captive_summary: GNL Quintero's own technical description of its four vaporizers shows the only gas-combustion equipment on site is the backup Submerged Combustion Vaporizer (SCV) -- a heat exchanger that burns natural gas to heat a demineralized-water bath for LNG regasification, used only as backup to the three primary seawater Open Rack Vaporizers (ORV). This is process heat, not electric power generation (same ground as Swinoujscie/Zeebrugge SCV settled NOs) -- there is no captive gas power plant at this terminal.
confirmed_how: GNL Quintero's own website (gnlquintero.com/terminal/vaporizadores/): 'El Terminal tiene cuatro Vaporizadores... Tres de ellos son de panel abierto (Open Rack Vaporizers, ORV)... En tanto, el Vaporizador de Combustion Sumergida (Submerged Combustion Vaporizer, SCV), opera como respaldo del sistema... Esta compuesto por intercambiadores de calor por los que circula GNL, los que estan sumergidos en una piscina con agua desmineralizada que es calentada mediante la combustion de gas natural.' (Translation: the SCV is a standby heat exchanger that heats a demineralized-water bath via natural-gas combustion to vaporize LNG -- explicitly a thermal/vaporization process, not electricity generation.) No other on-site gas-fired equipment (generators, turbines) is described anywhere on the operator's own site or in any secondary source reviewed (offshore-technology.com project profile, McDermott EPC profile).
